Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

particular adjective

fussy, hard to please

also fussy, picky, choosy, fastidious, fussy eater, snobbish

classical

Cic. Brut. 207: fastīdiōsior Crassus
Plaut. Mil. 4.6.18 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 158

fastīdiōsus, fastīdiōsa, fastīdiōsum

particular, fastidious, choosy

Fussiness itself is fastīdium, and to turn up one’s nose at a thing, fastīdīre: quod fastīdit quisque, what each one won’t eat (Phaedr. 3.7.23).

Other words

  • mōrōsus, mōrōsa, mōrōsum — particular, hard to please

    also used · classical · Suet. Jul. 45: circā corporis cūram mōrōsior (Lewis & Short: “particular, fastidious”); Cic. Or. 104: difficilēs ac mōrōsī

    Often “grumpy” as well (see “difficult”, of a person).

  • dēlicātus, dēlicāta, dēlicātum — fussy, spoilt, dainty

    also used · classical · Petr. 45.1: nōn dēbēmus dēlicātī esse; Plaut. Men. 1.2.10 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Antōnius, quī maximē expetēbātur, facilis in causīs recipiendīs erat; fastīdiōsior Crassus, sed tamen recipiēbat.

    Antonius, who was most in demand, was easy-going about taking on cases; Crassus was more particular, but took them all the same.Cic. Brut. 207

  • usque eō difficilēs ac mōrōsī sumus, ut nōbīs nōn satis faciat ipse Dēmosthenēs

    we are so particular and hard to please that not even Demosthenes satisfies usCic. Or. 104

  • fastīdientis stomachī est multa dēgustāre

    tasting a little of everything is the mark of a fussy stomachSen. Ep. 2.4

See also particular, difficult.
